scope: Read-only diagnosis of isolated resgrid-academy-oct25, fictional department51. No browser, HTTP/API request, application edit, support-pin change or database write.

read_only_database_observations.transaction: BEGIN READ ONLY; SELECT statements; ROLLBACK

root_cause.finding: Concurrent replacement cleanup can delete another in-flight upload, including the key finally stored on the type. Three same-second completed form submissions plus three inserted/deleted rows are consistent with this exact race.
root_cause.source_algorithm: UploadIconAsync inserts a new image, updates the owner type to that key, then DeleteSlotAsync deletes all other same-slot keys. Those operations use separate autocommit connections when no ambient unit of work exists; neither the service nor repository owns a replacement transaction/owner row lock.
root_cause.evidence_limit: Gateway logs establish the three concurrent submissions and table statistics establish insert/delete totals. Exact SQL interleaving was not logged. The retained deterministic in-memory reproduction demonstrates a permitted source execution with the observed orphan and counts; it does not invent a query trace.
not_indicated: image decode or PNG corruption (there are no bytes to decode)

deterministic_offline_reproduction.kind: in-memory source-operation model, not a live DB experiment

safest_fix_before_implementation: Use a database transaction for a complete replacement, beginning before ownership/slot serialization and before insertion. Serialize on the department-owned type row, using PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE or SQL Server equivalent UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK. All participating repository operations must share that connection and transaction.

Apply the same owner/slot serialization discipline to base uploads, variant uploads and removals, so no concurrent cleanup can remove another replacement. Preserve tenant scoping, existing authentication/authorization, immutable key semantics and variant independence.
On any failure roll back insertion, pointer update and cleanup together. Retain prior working reference. Avoid an in-process-only lock because multiple web/API instances can write concurrently.

Add a genuine concurrent-upload regression against an isolated test database. After overlapping replacements, every stored base key and returned active variant must resolve to retained nonempty PNG bytes; no cross-tenant/slot deletion. Existing single-operation mocked and DB tests do not exercise this schedule.

Separately consider preventing ordinary type-field updates from overwriting server-owned IconKey with a stale loaded value. This did not need to be assumed for the demonstrated replacement-cleanup race.
safe_operational_recovery_option: After normal UI access and deliberate disposal of duplicate pending form submissions, a single ordinary re-upload from one form can restore a valid reference. This would be recovery only, not proof that the concurrency defect is fixed. No recovery performed by this agent.
